Port S3 is built: the plan, the cost and the PDF in the browser copy

The answer first: on milled parts the browser copy now works out the same machine plan and cost drivers as the Python app, on every test file it can compare. The setups are separate cards that say what a tap does, as you approved (D-061). With your approval, I merge it now; S4 (pockets) starts in a new session.

Open the demo: tap two_sided_block, then Machining, then a setup; tap report_sample, then Cost, for the “(partial)” total. PR #36.

What you see

Is it the same as Python?

  • Quick set (77 files, every push): 77 the same. Before this slice, 23 of the 77 differed on the plan and cost.
  • Full set (290 files): 282 the same; 6 crash the Python app itself (old UMD files); 2 differ only in a few mesh points of the 3D view (bn_ball6 and nasty_cheese), as in S1 and S2.
  • The plan and cost are compared only on files with no pockets and no finding from a check not in this copy yet: 25 of the quick set's milled files. The rest wait for S4 and S5, and the screen says so.

Checks

  • All local checks passed: 926 service tests, 49 web tests, 79 browser tests on the Python app and 32 on the browser copy, and the quick parity.
  • A fresh reviewer read the build against the spec: 1 major and 6 minor findings. 6 are fixed. The major one was the setup card hiding its keyboard focus ring; it is now drawn inside the card, with a test. The 7th: the work copy's GitLab pipeline can't be tested until the move; its steps ran here on Node 22.
  • The big-plate memory test (J4) was not run (D-059).

What's left for you

  • Turn on GitHub Pages once (Settings, Pages, Source: GitHub Actions), if you haven't yet; then the public test copy updates on each merge.
  • The work copy is now possible: before it goes up, tell IT or your manager (D-055), and check whether the work GitLab has runners that can download packages.
  • Pockets come in S4, in a new session; that also removes the pocket line.
